utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gerxhaliu.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, and ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The cross-examination by Mr. Ivetic will continue in a moment. The -- I just remind you, as I did yesterday morning, that the solemn declaration which you took at the very beginning of your evidence on Monday continues to apply to your evidence today. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, I'd like to continue with the line of questioning that we'd started yesterday, and I'd like to direct your attention right now to the events you describe at paragraphs 28 through 31 of your written statement regarding the events of the 31st of May, 1999. Is it accurate to state that you never actually saw the persons who came to your cousin's house on that day, the armed persons who came to the house on that day?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. I did not see them leaving, and this is what I stated in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The translation I received says: "I did not see them leaving." Is it also correct that you did not see them arrive either, that you did not see them with your own eyes at any time?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the room, lying down, and when they called my wife, they addressed her in Serbo-Croatian, said to her: Come here. And she came to me, informed me, and I fled in the opposite direction and I did not turn my head back to look at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for clearing that up for me. Now, when we talk about the discovery and the identification of the bodies of your cousin and your uncle, Seladin, Xhemajl and Shaban, is it correct to state that it was actually the members -- the fighters of the UCK/KLA that first found these three bodies?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were about one kilometre further. I do not know who found them there, but what I know is that my father went there together with two other persons and brought them for burial. And I measured the distance. The bodies were found at exactly one kilometre distance from Seladin's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact that the bodies were found approximately 300 metres from a KLA check-point?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct because their bodies were, as I said, one kilometre far from Seladin's house. My father and two other persons went to pick them up, put them in a cart, and came back. And one of them then entered the house and saw the other members of Seladin's family executed inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your father, Sali Gerxhaliu, did he tell you that in fact that he had encountered KLA fighters who had moved the bodies, the three bodies?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could have been moved. I don't know. I didn't see that myself. I wasn't present there. However, I know that he brought them. And, as I said earlier, I had to remain in hiding for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not questioning that your father is the one who brought the bodies back. I'm trying to establish your knowledge of the scene that your father saw when he found the bodies with the KLA persons, and I'd like to ask you another question in that regard. Do you have knowledge of the fact that these KLA members had already collected the three bodies for burial with other KLA fighters, that they believed that these three bodies were of KLA fighters? Do you have any knowledge of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that these three bodies were spotted for the first time by some girls who came to inform us. They said to us: There are three bodies there. My cousin, Xhema's son in fact, went to speak with these girls and he informed us. And then my father went to pick up the bodies. Now, if they were really KLA soldiers, then they would have been in KLA uniforms. And the KLA would have picked them up. But the truth is what I've already told you, and I can only confirm things that I know for sure. I know that my father went there, took them in a cart, and brought them to the house, together with these two other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, your father, Sali Gerxhaliu, I'd like to put something forward to you, are you aware that your father executed a sworn statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, wherein he described that, in fact, KLA members had collected the bodies because they thought the victims were also KLA? Do you have knowledge of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that my father gave a statement and that my father collected the bodies. And my father is a person who actually knew better than KLA who these persons were. These were his cousins. And this should be clear, that he went there to pick them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The point I'm trying to reach, sir, is the fact that these three bodies were dressed in civilian clothing, and yet the KLA mistook them for KLA combatants. Does that in fact refresh your recollection as to whether it was possible for KLA combatants in the area to dress as civilians or in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already stated yesterday, and I will repeat it today, from the moment they took up arms, the KLA soldiers were always dressed in uniforms until they were demobilised when the NATO forces entered Kosova. As for others who supported the KLA, they were KLA supporters, indeed, but they were never armed and never wore a uniform. And please, how can then someone carrying a weapon allow for someone else to come and execute his entire family before his very eyes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm just trying to ascertain the facts pertaining to this incident, and I want to ask you another question. When your father brought the three bodies in the cart to the cemetery that day, isn't it a fact that the KLA persons who were present at the cemetery directed him to bring the nine other bodies as well, that is to say, isn't it a fact that the KLA had been the first on the scene at the Gerxhaliu house where the nine other bodies were located?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA moved up and down, communicated with the brigade on the other side of the railroad, on the other side of the Sitnica river, but the fact is that two girls spotted these bodies the first and they heard their execution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question is: What happened at the cemetery? Can you confine yourself to dealing with that question. Did the KLA intervene to give directions about the nine other bodies at the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only speak of things that I've seen myself and what I've heard. My father told me that he collected the bodies from the crime scene, brought them to the house --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, let's confine ourselves to the cemetery. Your statement says clearly: "We loaded the bodies onto two carts and took them to the family cemetery." So it sounds from the statement as if you were at the cemetery; so could you deal with that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the first and the second time that the police came from Vushtrri and issued a permission for the bodies to be buried, that's when we collected the bodies. On the second occasion, I went there together with my cousins. We put them in a cart, and then brought them to the cemetery where the bodies can be found even today. There there were no KLA except for family members who attended the burial ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What day was that that you went to the cemetery? Am I correct that you did not go to the cemetery with your father with the three original bodies, the three bodies of your cousin and your uncle and your cousin's son?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: For these three bodies, I already told you that it was my father with two other persons who went to collect them. Then Sheribane went to the police. And after they received this permission for their burial, that's when we took the bodies for burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you a little bit about the process by which the authorities were contacted. You had said hat there was some discussion amongst the family members as to whether or not the police should be contacted. I want to ask you another question. Was it the KLA that encouraged you to contact the police to report these killings?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. And the KLA was not involved in this. This was a decision of the inhabitants who lived there in that neighbourhood around Rashiq. There were people who would often go to the town to do shopping, among them Sheribane that I mentioned, and she went to report the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you another question then. Were the police notified upon the insistence of your father, Sali Gerxhaliu? Was he the moving force for the notification to be made to the authorities?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us together, we all agreed that the Yugoslav police in Vushtrri should be informed. This was a consensus reached by all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if I could have you focus on the event when you said that the -- that the authorities came out there, the police, and the court personnel came out to do an investigation. Did you personally eye-witness any of the activities of this investigative team on the 31st of May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already mentioned it earlier, that I had no chance to contact -- to have any contact with them when they came. So the first time when they came with a team of this female doctor that I mentioned and the other investigators, it is only my father who contacted with them. They asked my father about me, and he told them that I was allegedly in Macedonia. On the second occasion when they came to issue this permission for the burial --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Go ahead, you can -- I mean -- you can finish.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So after they issued this permission for the burial, I was kind of certain that the police will not come back. And then I went back there to help, and we collected all the bodies from the room, put them in a cart, and took them to the cemetery for burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What I'm trying to establish, sir, is all your information and testimony where you talk about the persons who were present from this investigative team and the actions they undertook, is all that information and testimony second-hand, that is to say material that you found out about from other persons?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The doctor, Natalia Tasi, asked my father about me. And I heard from my father that they took photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's so obvious, Mr. Ivetic, that that's the case. You're losing perspective in this cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I should advise everyone that as of the end of this week we are going to have to reconsider how things are progressing time-wise in this trial and look at what the prospects are of conducting it within a reasonable time. They're not looking good at the moment. I would urge you to maintain perspective in your cross-examination on what is really important.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it a fact that on May 31st, 1999, there was a battle between elements of the KLA and Serb forces in your village of Donja Sudimlja?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I heard about it. I never heard about this thing before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you talked earlier in your testimony - I believe it was on Monday - that previously reported crimes had been ignored by the authorities. Now, I found no reference to this in your statement apart from the Prosecution's opening line of questioning. Could you please give us details when and to whom did you report previous alleged crimes that were not investigated by the authorities?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Previous alleged crimes that were not investigated by the authorities, I can't give you any information about this because I arrived in the village later -- before, two days, two.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are other witnesses who can testify about other crimes. I can only testify about the things that I know. I know that there are witnesses who testified to crimes that were committed on 14th of May and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now we've established you do not have direct knowledge of that. If I can return you just for a couple of questions and then we'll be finished. I'd like to clear up a few points relating to the night of May the 2nd, 1999, that we had discussed previously. Now, first of all, you already told us that with respect to the first group of armed men that approached the convoy at 5.00 p.m. in the evening, that apart from the colour of their uniforms it was impossible for you to distinguish any emblems or insignia on the uniforms. I would like to ask you a question with respect to the subsequent groups of armed men. Would the same be true for those subsequent groups of armed men that came later that night, that is to say that you could not identify any emblems or insignia on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never given a statement of this kind. What happened happened on the 2nd of May. On the 3rd of May, they returned. I heard that the KLA forces took positions, and the burial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the answer -- is the simple answer that you can't -- sorry, that you could not identify any emblems or insignia on any of the groups that approached on the 2nd of May after 5.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I heard yes in Albanian, but it hasn't been translated but it was --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I heard "po" as well, so -- and I'm sure the transcript will reflect that later on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we talked about just -- by just one question about the vehicles that came at 11.45 p.m. Yesterday you said that you could not see the colour of these vehicles. How is it that you knew or assumed that these vehicles -- that two of these vehicles were police vehicles?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was moonlight. It is true that you cannot distinguish colours clearly at night. But I knew the shape of the Zastava 101 make vehicles, I knew the shape and form of the APCs and Pinzgauers and other vehicles used by the police and army. They were all together in the same column.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You had not seen these police vehicles prior -- on -- earlier that day, had you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I was like half hidden and I couldn't see them clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me just ask you -- I have two final questions on a final topic, sir, regarding the period when you left Kosovo-Metohija. First of all, can you confirm for us that you did not ultimately leave the province due to any orders given by anyone, but rather you and your relatives arranged, through another relative, to have a bus evacuate you from Kosovo-Metohija. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's accurate. I was afraid what would happen to my family since Seladin's family became a sacrifice. So that was an issue of to be or not to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And could you also confirm for us that your family sought refuge in Serbia and Montenegro and remained there until the NATO forces entered Kosovo-Metohija and then you returned home?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Ulqin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Maybe we could prepare exhibit -- Defence Exhibit 3D63 while I start with my first question so we have it ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, Mr. Ivetic just asked you about whether or not you saw the policemen that came in the direction of your house on the 31st of May, and you said you did not. At the time, did your wife say that the police was coming?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My wife had seen them coming, and she spoke with them. They called her, told her: Come here. And they also called on Florie, my wife's cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Gerxhaliu. Just to clear that one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we see the exhibit that I just mentioned, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the third paragraph on this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Somewhere in the third paragraph there's mention of a school. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think in the third paragraph. It should probably be approximately on the middle of the screen somewhere. It's in Cyrillic so I cannot fully assist.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in Cyrillic, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And you can see "school." Do you know what school is mentioned in this text?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me read the paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third paragraph, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the second?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the English version it looks like it's the third, but maybe it's the second in reality. Can you see the word "school"? Oh yeah, I can -- if it can help I can see a number that I can understand. It says M61/557, and a little further on in that sentence probably the reference to the school would be. So it looks like it's actually the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On this document it's 618-557.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm -- so it's the end of the second paragraph probably.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I found it. So around 11.35 hours between the villages of Gornja and Donja Sudimlja fire was opened at an official vehicle -- yes, yes, I found it. Registration plate number 16 -- I think it's a primary school there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, if you are coming from Vucitrn and moving in the direction of your house, could you describe where the school is, please?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you go from the direction of Vushtrri, the school is about half kilometre far from the place where the three bodies of Seladin, Xhemajl, and the other person were found. The direction of Studime e Eperme.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: So on the other side, further away. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, yes, further away in the direction of Studime e Eperme. It's about two kilometres from my house, between one and a half and two kilometres from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Gerxhaliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Next I'd like if we could see Exhibit 3D70, please. It appears, Your Honours, that that document is not in e-court. I have to say I don't remember whether a hard copy was handed around yesterday, but that's probably the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, in the interest of time, I think we should just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry about that, Mr. Gerxhaliu --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Oh, here we have it, but we only have an English translation of the document. Do we have the B/C/S version? There we have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Could we look at the first paragraph. I'll just get my copy out again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: In the -- the last sentence says in the English version: "In the area of Bajgora village and the Shala district were members of -- were members of Siptar terrorists of this -- sorry, Siptar terrorist gang launched a fierce attack launching all kinds of weapons against members of the PJP ..." And so on. Now, Bajgora and Shala district, is that the area where the Serb forces had broken through the KLA lines on the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's where the KLA line was broken through, and it fell on the 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now last I'd like to show about a minute and a half of Exhibit P4 that we saw some parts of yesterday on the monitor. And, Dr. Gerxhaliu, we're just going to let the film run, and then I have two questions about what is seen on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, in the first part of what we saw showed a number of bodies on the ground. Yesterday you were asked from the same video to identify whether a number of people were maybe KLA fighters. Now, on the short sequence we just saw, did any of the people on the ground resemble the KLA fighters that you had been seeing at the military hospital you were working at?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were all civilians. As you could see for yourselves, they had no uniforms on. Some of them were my cousins. They were executed at short distance. They were beaten, maltreated. This film was made on the 13th when -- the 3rd --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- when the burial took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And that probably answered my second question, which was: The graves we saw, are they the graves where you were attending the burials of the victims of the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI GERXHALIU [Resumed]
utterances.text: The burial began on the 3rd of May, the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Thank you, Dr. Gerxhaliu. I am --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Marcussen, is there a way of identifying the passage of film that you've shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, it was -- I'm sorry. It was 16 minutes -- from 16 minutes, 15 seconds to 18 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I believe that yesterday my colleague did not enter P4 into evidence. I would like to tender that at this point so it's on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it becomes part of the evidence insofar as it's used, so it has in fact entered evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I don't have any further questions to this witness. I do have some housekeeping matters relating to the evidence of the witness, but my questioning is over. So maybe Your Honours have some questions, otherwise I can deal with the housekeeping matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What are the housekeeping matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It's basically just some references to documents that have been incomplete, and I thought we should maybe mention the Prosecution's identification number of the photographs so it's clear on the record what it was we talked about yesterday when the Bench saw some photographs. Maybe I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, they didn't -- they weren't entered. They certainly are not part of the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Certainly not. Maybe I am paranoid after having been in -- working in the appeals section of the Office of the Prosecutor. But often when we look at transcripts, later on issues arise as to what had been looked at in court, so that was the only purpose of mentioning that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, you were invited if was there any issue on this to reach some agreement with the Defence about how you might deal with it or address it yourself if it is an issue. But there was -- as I understood the position, there was no issue over the identification of 12 victims. That was confirmed by Mr. Visnjic yesterday, and therefore I see no need to complicate the process with the photographs. We've seen them, but they don't need to be introduced for that -- for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm certainly not suggesting they should be part of the evidence, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we don't need to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Then maybe I could just do one thing to make the record complete in one regard. My colleague Mr. Visnjic at page 2.560, line 22, referred to a statement. The number there should be K0016 -- excuse me 8614, just where that is complete. The rest we can take note of in different ways. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's a document which is not an exhibit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: That is correct. But, again, the thought is the same. We need maybe in future to find out what it is they have been talking about in -- during court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Dr. Gerxhaliu, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming again to the Tribunal to give it. You're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you as well, Your Honours. And I hereby send you the regards of my co-villagers as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, I gather you have two matters to raise with us?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. First of all, the first matter relates to the next witness who has previously been referred to as Witness K13. Protective measures had been granted originally in the Milosevic case, IT-02-54, on the 22nd of March, 2002, in which he was granted the pseudonym of K13 and facial distortion for testimony. In the passage of time, Your Honour, this witness has relocated. He's older now, he's 17 and a half years old, and we've discussed the matter with him. In the present circumstances, he no longer desires nor do we think it's necessary that he have protective measures, and we propose that he testify openly, under his true name, and without any other protective measures. And we would like to request that those prior measures be withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, that's an application, Mr. Hannis, which will be under Rule 75(G) to us as the second -- the Chamber dealing with the second proceedings in a situation where no Chamber remains seized of the first proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we have a free hand?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's my understanding of the rule, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. And -- yeah, well, let's deal with that first of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, in light of what you have said, Mr. Hannis, this Trial Chamber will now rescind all existing protective measures in relation to this witness, and that gives any future Trial Chamber an absolutely free hand should it be necessary to consider protective measures at any later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now give me the name of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: His first name is Dren, D, as in David, r-e-n.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And his last name is Caka, C-a-k-a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this is a witness who will give live testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And who will lead that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will lead that witness, Your Honour. And his testimony relates to pargarphs 72(h), 73, 74, 75(g), and Schedule G of the indictment relating to killings at the Milos Gilic Street in Djakovo on the 2nd of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And your second application?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The second application, Your Honour, refers to a witness Bajram Bucaliu who was scheduled to be the fourth witness, or the third witness after this one, and we don't anticipate we will get to him until next week. He is from Urosevac, Ferizaj municipality. We had originally proposed him as a live witness. Upon proofing him yesterday morning, we determined that it might be most efficient to proceed by using him as a 92 bis (D) witness. He testified at greater length than the average crime base witness in the Milosevic trial, and his testimony covers practically everything I would have asked him if we had proceeded live. We notified the Defence of that by e-mail that that's what we were proposing to do. Rule 92 bis (E) I believe, Your Honour, requires us to make the application 14 days in advance and allows the Defence seven days in which to respond. However, Rule 127 permits Your Honours to shorten the time-period, if you think there's good cause shown or if it's in the interests of justice. We would indicate to you that we think this evidence is appropriate for 92 bis (D) --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're assuming cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's see what the Defence position is. Mr. O'Sullivan, is there a joint position on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I don't believe there's any opposition to this request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, so we can foreshorten the time -- the notice and deal with this application just now?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let's consider that then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there being no opposition from any of the accused, we shall waive the requirements of notice, the period of notice, in this case, and we shall grant the application made by Mr. Hannis so that the witness may give evidence as a witness tendered in terms of Rule 92 bis (D).

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will ask him a few questions live, and in particular there's one matter relating to the train log that he helped keep as part of the transport of trains through the station, then I think it will be helpful to have me asking a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So his evidence, then, will in large part be tendered in terms of 92 bis (D) and he will attend and be subject to cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can we have your witness? Is he on the way?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm told that he is now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Caka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hi, how are you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you now make the solemn declaration by reading aloud from the document which will now be placed in front of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please be seated. Are you intending to give evidence in English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, you're going to be asked questions by a number of counsel representing, first of all, the Prosecution and then representing each of the accused. The important thing for us is that you listen very closely and carefully to the question and you answer the question that's put to you. Sometimes that can appear to be difficult because you want -- you may want to tell an account of something, but the way we deal with it in the system that we follow here is to allow each of the counsel to identify what it is they want you to tell us about. If we feel we need to -- if we feel we need to know more, we will ask you more questions at the end. But it will help us all if you try to confine your answers to the particular point that you're asked about. Now, please try your best to do that. The first counsel to ask questions will be for the Prosecution, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could you tell us your name, please.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My name is Dren.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And your last name?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Caka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you spell both those names for us, please.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: First name is D-r-e-n, last name is C-a-k-a.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And since you're testifying in English today and I'm speaking English, I would ask you to try and have a pause between the end of my question and the beginning of your answer, so the interpreters can keep up with us as they're translating into the other three languages that are being used, okay?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How old are you?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I'm 17 and will be 18 on December 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you speak English now. Do you also speak Albanian?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I speak Albanian fluently, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I -- sorry, I couldn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you Albanian by birth?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And from the time you were born until 1999, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I lived in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In March 1999 then, by my math, you would have been 10 years old, 10 and a half?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who did you live with at that time?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: After the incident happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Up until April of 1999, who did you live with?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I lived with my grandfather, my grandmother, my parents and uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you give us their names, please. Grandma and grandpa first.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Grandma is Xhemajla Caka -- sorry, Nakije Caka; grandfather is Xhemil Caka; my uncle's name is Nehat Caka; my dad's name is Ali Caka; my mother's name is Valbona Caka; and my sisters' name is Dalina Caka, Delvina Caka, Diona Caka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How old were your sisters in March of 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall where in Gjakove your family lived?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I can say the old name, but I don't know the new street name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Tell us the old street name.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Millosh Giliq.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall a pool hall on Millosh Giliq street?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Whose pool hall was that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was Luli Vejsa's.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How far from there did you live approximately?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Two houses away.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would next like to show you an exhibit, P275, please. In a moment, Mr. Caka, a photograph -- an aerial photograph will come up on your screen. And my first question for you about that will be if you recognise the area that's in that picture, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And what is that area?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: This is -- it was my street and my house, I can see my house, and the house the incident happened in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In a minute I'll have the usher hand you a pen that's attached to the monitor with which you can actually touch the screen and draw on it. First of all, could you draw a circle around the pool hall that you mentioned and put a P inside the circle.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did Luli Vejsa have a house nearby?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you draw a circle around the house and put an H inside it for his house.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you see on that photo the house where your family lived?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you draw a circle around that? And put a C in it.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Did you know any of your other neighbours?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No -- well, I know who they are but I can't think of it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was there a policeman that lived in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you see his house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would you draw a circle around it?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And could you put POL inside that circle for us.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we have a screen shot of that and mark that as --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one second before you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The one that's marked H, did you mean to circle only the part which appears to have been destroyed or at least which does not have a roof, or do you mean to take in the parts which are at the street and which do appear to have a roof?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the H is just the roof the house that the incident happened in. The whole house, that's -- you mean the whole -- like, with a yard and everything is just a big circle, but only the house is the H.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but does that house extend out to the street where the car -- where the vehicle is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we give that the next IC number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this picture will become Exhibit IC24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Caka, I would to ask you, do you recall when the NATO bombing started? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I don't know, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the night of April 1st and early morning of April 2nd, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's the night that it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On that date, where were you and your family staying?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: In a basement underneath the pool hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how long had you been staying there at that time, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: On that day or the whole time that I went there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Before that day, had you been staying there for some period of time?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: We had been staying there about four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And why were you staying at that location?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Because we thought if -- in case of any bombings it would be a safer place to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware of any -- any disturbances or problems in your immediate neighbourhood the day or two before the incident that you have been talking about?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, about a day or two before I was playing with my sister in my own house, we were playing just marbles, and a police officer came by the house and he told us to get inside. And that's the only thing that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In the basement -- who was staying in the basement, how many people, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: 20 people. I was the 21st person.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Any men in this group of 21?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, there was a man, but he was about 60, so he was an old man.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how about the rest of the group besides him and you?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It was just women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the basement, did you have any idea of how big it was?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I would say about half of the size of this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was it one big room or were there separate rooms that you stayed in?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It was just one big room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where were your father and uncle and the other men related to these families staying while you all were staying in the basement?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: They were staying in the same property as us. They were keeping guard because the police officers, they would say -- they said they were mostly looking for men; they wouldn't harm women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So on the night of April 1st and April 2nd, what men related to your family and the other people staying there were on the property elsewhere, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: After they left?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No. When you went to -- well, what time did you all go down to the basement on that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Just early afternoon, like early evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know if the men were still around on the premises?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: They would stay up all night. They would take turns on getting some rest, but there was always somebody up to keep guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what time you went to sleep that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was given sleeping pills so I can sleep, and I would say about 11.45 I was about asleep, 11.45 to 12.00. I'm not exactly too sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. When did you wake up or when were you woken up?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was woken up about 2.00 in the morning, around that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how did that happen? Who woke you up?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My mom woke me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What did she say?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: She said: Wake up, police officers are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: We tried to keep quiet, and we heard kind of a loud noise, but we didn't know what it was. And the door opened up and there was Serbian police officers and they told us: Get out. They were talking mostly Serbian but they were also talking Albanian. They were saying: Are you with the UCK, the KLA, Kosovo Liberation Army, and we said: No, we're just trying to be safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me slow you down a minute. In the basement were there -- was the basement below ground level or were there any windows that you could see out of?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: There was only two windows on the side facing towards the house and we had them boarded shut so you can't see in or see out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how many entrances or exits to the basement were there?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. When your mom woke you up, was the door open or shut?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No, it was shut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was it locked?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It wasn't locked.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And how was it that the police came in? Did they knock?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: They just opened it. They didn't knock; they just opened it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, you said they were speaking some in Serbian and some in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did anyone in your group understand Serbian?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, quite a lot of -- my mom, she understood it, but not really a lot. But there was a -- like Dushi, she understand Serbian quite well, and -- but I didn't have time to ask her what they were saying and also I was too young, and I don't think she would have given me an answer. But what they said in Albanian, that I can understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What do you recall being said in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Are you guys with UCK? And we said: No, we're just trying to be safe. Like, please leave us alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How many men were there?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: There was -- in the beginning there was about six, but in the end there was only three I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you recall how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: They were dressed in police uniforms, dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Was it a solid colour or some kind of pattern?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It was -- it was patterned. It wasn't just blue. It was blue and blackish.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Had you seen these kind of uniforms before?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, I've seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where had you seen them before?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: You see policemen, if they pull you over if you're driving, or if you see policemen pull somebody else over, you see them out of their car and you always see the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Where did you all go from the basement?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that was whose house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was Luli's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The one that you marked with an H on the photograph we saw before?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did all six of the policemen come with you?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No. Two -- well, three, sorry, were at the door where the car was on fire. And as soon as we got up into the front porch they -- they walked away. I couldn't see them anymore. Because I turned my head for only a slight second. I looked back. They were gone. But there was only three there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think I'd like to have IC24 put up again to ask a couple more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On the -- on the way from the basement to the house, was there any conversation that you could understand?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did these men have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, they were heavily armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Each one of them have some sort of weapon?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah. They had machine-guns, AK-47s, and secondary guns, just normal hand-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In the -- the photograph that you marked before, I have a question for you. You mentioned there was a car burning. Whose car was that and where was it located?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was Behar's car.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was it on the street?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No. It was against the door of -- the front entrance door to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you talking about the front entrance house to the building or to the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: To the yard. Like, where you go on the property.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you take the pen again.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if you could, with a small circle perhaps, draw and put in an A for automobile where the burning car was.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the gate to the property --

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Right below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It was right below.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what kind of gate was that, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It was -- it was a steel gate, like steel -- it was doors but they were steel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the car was parked behind it?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, closing them shut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Between the basement and the house when you were walking, in addition to the burning car, was there any other source of light?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't need that any further at this time. I guess I need to mark this as the next IC number because we've added to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit IC25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What happened when you got to Luli's house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, on our way there from the basement we first entered the door. They -- Luli is younger. The third daughter, she goes to open the door, and one police officer fired because the door was shut and missed her and we went inside the house. They sat us all around into the living-room. And some people were out in the hallway. About three or four, I'm not too sure, were in the hallway. And in the living-room, we were just sitting there, talking, and Flaka gets up to make tea. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you for a minute there. I'm going to ask you a couple more questions and then show you a diagram. Among this group of six policemen, did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I think one kind of looked like my -- the neighbour, the police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: But he was kind of hiding his face and he didn't come inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P2279, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, before today in the past when talking about this event, at one time were you given a diagram of the floor plan of the house where this occurred?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [No verbal answer].

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you shown one and asked to make a drawing on it?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And do you have something up on the screen now in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It's a picture of the rooms in the house and the porch and everything -- how it was in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I see your name at the bottom and a date. Did you write that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And in the diagram, we see what appears to be four rooms and a bathroom. Is that how the house was at that time?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I see --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know if we can enlarge a little bit the lower two-thirds of that exhibit to get a better look at the numbers in the rooms. Okay. That's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I don't know how big that is on your screen, Mr. Caka, but can you see -- there are some circles with the letter A and B beside them and some dots with the numbers -- it appears to be 1 through 10. Did you make those markings?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what those are -- first of all, let me ask you about the circle and the -- and the letter A on what appears to be the front step area. Who is that or what is that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And B?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Also a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And inside the room in the lower right corner in the doorway that appears to be another circle. Who or what does that represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The letter B going to the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And so that's the same policeman moving from the front to the --

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- to the room?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah. But there was also one but I didn't see where he was outside so I've never marked that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So there was a third one in or around the house at that time?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I think he was on the bottom right corner, close to the window, because shots were fired through the window, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you tell us about the numbers one at a time -- well, let me ask you this: Is it easier for you to tell us the sequence of events and then go back and tell us what the numbers represent, or is it easier to describe what the numbers represent and then tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Either way it's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't you tell us the sequence and then we can talk about the numbers, or maybe we can do it at the same time as you go along. What happened once you got inside?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Inside the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, they walked us in the living-room, and there was a couple, three or four people, I'm not so sure, in the hallway, because it's been such a long time now. And -- but I was in the room, I was behind Dushi, I remember her name. Most other people I don't remember their name. It's been quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And who was Dushi, was she a child or an adult?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No, she was about 47 years old at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: And they sat us down. We were just talking about, and Flaka decides to go and make tea. And as she's walking, a police officer kind of like pushes her and fires and she's gone. And her mom, around the corner of the door, ran out and she -- she was gone too. And also then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When you say "she was gone," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Like, she got shot, too, right after her daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Then the -- where the number 2 is, that was Luli's wife and his baby daughter. The baby daughter got shot first. Then Luli's wife dropped the baby and then she got shot. Then afterwards it was my mother, and she was changing my baby sister's diaper, and she got shot in the back and fell right on top of my baby sister. And then afterwards they shot all the way at the bottom right corner. Arlind was there, and my sister was there, my older sister. And after that they fired at the closet which started to burn the house on fire. And it was all -- it was smoking, and my sister passed me her glove, and she said: Here, take this. Like, before -- because my other sister was nearby -- but then I don't know, she kind of ran away. It's hard. I really have to think about it, but right now at the moment I don't really remember it quite well. And in the hallway, I don't know which one got shot first, I don't know which one got shot afterwards, I don't know, because I wasn't there to see. But after, in the end, I decided to get up. And Arlind, Luli's son, was still breathing but I can tell that he's been shot a lot of times, and I tried to go over there and try to help him. As soon as I spoke one word, then there was no more breathing. Then from there I went across to try to help my baby sister because she hasn't gotten shot, but my mom was a little bit heavy, and my -- I only had my bad arm because my right arm, I was shot, and it was broken, so there's nothing I could do. And from there I took off my jacket, I went in the hallway, and I lied down, pretended like I was dead there too. And for about two, three minutes, from there, from there I went into the room where -- it was Luli's bedroom. I went there and lied down. The windows were open, so I could breathe a little bit. So I stayed there about five or six minutes, I'm not too sure. And from then I jumped over the window. When I jumped over the window, I went all the way to the top left corner because there's a door there, as you can see. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Is that a door?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, that's a door.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: And I tried to make way through there, but I looked around the house and I see -- I saw all those three police officers who were doing this. They were there smoking. So I said: If I go this way they might see me. And Luli had a pool hall, so there was a lot of cases of beer, but the cases in our country are plastic. So I stacked them up and I jumped over the wall where you can see the circle -- not bunch of circles on top of the house, but the other circle, that's me jumping over the wall. I went through this little road that's like on the side of the house. I went to this place where they had firewood. And behind there it's like a wall. We broke down so we can go through each other's houses so we don't have to go through the main street. I went through there. I went through a another wall, and then I was in the second person's house before my house. And there was a lot of wood there, too, but then it was like a whole wall -- like, not just a circle, but like one side of the wall was all off, and I saw my aunt there. And as soon as I saw my aunt, she kind of ran away. Maybe she thought I was the police because she just saw me from the corner of her eye, so I wasn't too sure. Then I was kind of yelling help. And she came back and she's like: Hi, Dren? And I said, like: Yes. And she said: What happened? And I said: Oh, everyone is gone. Everyone's dead. And she said: No, I think you've had a bad dream. I said: No, I don't think I've had a bad dream because it just happened right before my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there, Mr. Caka, for a minute and go back and ask you some more questions about the diagram. You mentioned that Flaka was the first one to be shot?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How old was she, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was she an adult? Teenager?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I think about teenager.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the diagram, do you have a number for her?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It says number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And where were you sitting when the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was sitting right close to the window where -- it's a figure -- kind of looks like a person where his leg ends, the left leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see. All right. And could you see who was shooting?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, it was the man right by the door, and then also some shots were fired through the window, but I couldn't see who was doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you yourself shot?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where did you get hit?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I got shot right in the arm, right arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did it -- did it go through your arm or hit the bone?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It hit the bone and it bounced right out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In the diagram on the left side, outside the house, there are three circles. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Three circles, that's the police officers after I left the house. That were smoking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And where was the dresser or the closet that you described as igniting on fire? Where would that be in this diagram?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It's right beside the television, where it says "TV" on the bottom right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned that your older sister handed you a scarf or a glove?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: A glove.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What was that for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: So it can kind of help me breathe a bit better, so I don't have direct smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. And number 2 you said was whom?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was Luli's wife and her daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How old was the daughter, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I think she's -- was around the same age as my baby sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Number 3?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Number 3, that was Flaka's mother that ran around because she was on the other side of the door and then she was the second one that got shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Number 4 and number 5 in the corner?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Number 4 and number 5, that was Arlind, which is Luli's son, and my sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Number 6 and 7 in the other corner?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was my mom and my other baby sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: How old was your baby sister?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My baby sister, she had turned 2 on April 1st, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You mention your mom was shot and fell on top of her?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But you believe she was still alive after --

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, because I can hear her cry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You tried to help her?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I tried to help her. My mom was a little bit heavy, and also I was 10 years old and my good arm wasn't in use, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in the hallway 8 and 9?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That was Behar's wife and her son. They were kind of hugging and they were both shot and they were dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Number 10?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Number 10, that was Luli's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there were 20 people in all besides yourself, correct, but you didn't have a chance to see or don't know where they were?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Luli -- the first girl that opened the door at the beginning, when they were taking us from basement, after they shot down the door she wasn't hit because she ran away. And my other sister, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I very briefly interrupt, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Number 6 and 7 you took together but they are actually some distance apart. Tell us again who number 6 and 7 represent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mom and my baby sister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So they are on opposite sides of the room, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I believe 6 and 7 are in the left-hand corner of the room. The number may have to be blown up better to see it. But it's 4 and 5 in the right-hand corner, and in the left-hand corner I think that's a 6 and a 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I now follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, before the cabinet or the closet caught on fire or was ignited when it was shot, did -- were there any other sources of light inside the house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: There was candlelight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know when or how the candles had been lit, who lit the candles?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Flaka's mother was lighting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I think that's all I have for this diagram. I want to go then back to Exhibit P275, if we could have a clean version of 275 again, I want to have you make some marks on this one for us, if you would, Mr. Caka. This is the aerial photograph of the neighbourhood. And you've indicated to us where the house was. Could you use the pen on this photograph to show us where you went when you left the house to where you went and saw the police, and then where you reversed track and went toward your aunt's house.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, that's my house, but my aunt was there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: First of all, I was in this room when everything happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: From there I exited, I lied down in the hall, and I stayed there about four or five minutes. And then from there I went into the room, and the windows were all open, so I stayed there probably about six, and the other one, I think, I don't know, four, five, three, I'm not too sure. And afterwards I exit out of this window, I jumped out of this window right here. And after I jumped out of the window, I walked all across to here, and then there was one, two, three police officers smoking there. And I looked slightly on my left side, and I saw them there, and I thought: Well, if I go through the door, they might see me. So I back traced to about halfway, right here. I stacked the beer casings, and I jumped over the wall that's there. And then afterwards, I ran through, and there was an opening right here. And then it kind of went like this but you can't see it from the house. And there's the whole wall that was kind of not just a hole, it was like the whole thing almost kind of broken. And then my aunt was on this corner waiting for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we give that an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit IC26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would like to tender Exhibit 275 and IC24, 25, 26, and the diagram 2279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, it's probably a good time to break off --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- so that you can commence fresh --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- after our break. So we will break now and we'll resume at five minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, you've explained to us how you got out of the house and where you went, and you met your aunt outside your house. Can you tell us briefly what happened after that. You had been shot in the arm and were bleeding. What -- what did you and your aunt do then?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My aunt still didn't believe it, so the first room in the back we call the fire room where we make stuff like food in the summer -- I mean in the winter time. And I went through there. My aunt started walking a little bit faster than me and I kind of, like, fainted. And she came back, she says: Are you okay? I said: Oh, yes, I'm fine but I've lost a lot of blood. I've been shot. She says: Quit saying that. You've only had a bad dream. And we went through, we passed by my uncle's room, and we went in the kitchen, and my grandfather and my grandma and my uncle were there. And they said: So what happened? I said: Oh, everyone's gone, everyone's been shot dead, and I've been shot in the arm. My grandfather is like: No, you haven't. I'm like: Take a look at my arm. Then he's like: Oh, my God. And he cut it with a knife, cut my sleeves with a knife and then tied my arm. We went in the back to my uncle's room. I lied there. We were only with candlelight, and every time we heard noises, we would just turn off the candle. And it was like that all night. I tried to eat something but I couldn't because the after-taste from all the smoke in the house is not really good. And we stayed there all night. And then in the morning my dad had came back -- well, my grandfather and my aunt were taking me to the hospital. They put a blanket around me, put me on my grandfather's bicycle, and they were pushing me all the way to the hospital. As I left, I told my dad, I'm like -- I gave him a hug and a kiss, and he said that he would see me to the other side, to Albania, Tirana. And I told him: Please come with me. He says: Oh, we're going on foot and you're going to be driven there. So we left off, and as we were going to the hospital, we ran into some police officers --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Who took you to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My grandfather and my aunt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And how did you go? On foot?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No, they put me on top of a bicycle and they were pushing me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. What happened when you got to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: So there was -- there was a Serbian soldier there, and he was -- he was a nice guy and he said: What happened? We have told him. My grandfather said: He got hurt, he got shot. And he said: I'm so sorry to hear this. He says: We're not the best kind of people. He says: We shouldn't be hurting women and children. They have nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you get treated at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah. They only took an X-ray of my arm and they wrapped it around, but it wasn't like the normal wrapping you would do when your arm was broken. Just kind of wrapped around with a sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
